Cerberus: Cerberus is a massive three-headed dog charged with guarding the gates of the Underworld to prevent the dead from escaping. He is a magnificent beast, companion of Hades and Zagreus.
When Zagreus left the House for the first time, Cerberus threw a tantrum that wrecked the House's lounge area.
Once Zagreus reaches the Temple of Styx, Cerberus guards its exit. Zagreus must find a Satyr Sack, Cerberus's favorite snack, as a bribe to leave the area.
Once he has been defeated, he'll run off to be with Hades in Tartarus.

Cerberus - Datos generales: Title: Hound of Hell
Alias: Infernal Beast Infernal Cerberus
Type: Animal
Affiliation: House of Hades
Keepsake: Old Spiked Collar
Parents: Typhon
Siblings: Charybdis, Lernaean Hydra, Aetos, Canine, Spawn of Typhon, Twins of Typhon, and Erymanthian Boar
Relations: Hades (Owner) Persephone (Owner) Zagreus (Owner) Melinoë (Owner)
Voice: Solo, Higgins, Regis, Marzipan

Cerberus - Characteristics and Personality: Cerberus is the guardian of the Underworld and the faithful companion of master Hades. Despite his intimidating reputation, he now serves more as a pet than anything else in the House of Hades.
Cerberus is a gentle, helpful, and playful dog. He has offered his companionship and protection to Zagreus when wore only diapers, swearing him eternal loyalty. Cerberus enjoys typical dog play, such as fetching, which can cause quite a bit of massive destruction. He loves Zagreus so much that he destroyed the lounge when Zagreus attempted to leave the Underworld for the first time.

Cerberus - Characteristics and Personality: Hades rewards Cerberus for his faithful work by allowing him to stay at home, but it is Cerberus who rewards Hades after a long day of work. He is reliable and cannot disobey his master's orders, but he can sometimes be persuaded with a simple bone.

Cerberus - Characteristics and Personality: Cerberus patrols the shores of the Styx to prevent strangers from entering or residents from leaving. It is possible to pet Cerberus (although only one of his heads enjoys pets) and indeed necessary to unlock certain improvements from the House Contractor. He can be needy, and when he becomes anxious, he may carelessly destroy the lounge, making it unavailable for immediate use. But overall, he is a great companion and is well-loved by all members of his family.
After being corrupted by Chronos, Cerberus becomes a marauding beast consumed with rage and sorrow.

Cerberus - Physical description: Cerberus is a formidable, three-headed guard dog depicted as a large and imposing creature, towering over many tall characters, including Hades. He possesses bright red fur, and each of his heads features a distinct green nose and a salivating tongue with an orange-to-yellow gradient. This unique coloration may suggest the presence of acid or lava, further emphasizing of docile Cerberus's intimidating nature.

Cerberus - Hades: Upon taking notice of Zagreus' absence within the House of Hades, Cerberus became agitated and upset, frustratingly destroying the Lounge.
When Zagreus reaches the Temple of Styx he encounters Cerberus guarding the gate to the surface. Zagreus ultimately can't bring himself to fight Cerberus and opts to bribe him with a sack filled with an unknown content that Cerberus loves which allows him to leave the Underworld without fighting his canine friend.

Cerberus - Affinity: Cerberus' affinity gauge maxes out at 9 hearts. The 7th affinity gauge will be locked until Zagreus pets him at least 20 times (pets given before the final favor lock was added to the game are not counted, so fortunately you must pet him another 20 times). Petting him 10 times earns the Three-Headed Boy achievement, which is an indicator that you're at least halfway there.
If affinity is maxed out with Cerberus, there will be unique text above his keepsake. this text states: "from Cerberus; you share a ferocious bond" as well as "the hound of hell has entrusted all his loyalty in his master, and his master's son".

Cerberus - Trivia: - The voice "actors" for Cerberus were the pet dogs of the devs from Supergiant Games. Higgins, one of the dogs that voiced Cerberus sadly passed away on January 24, 2020.
- Two of Cerberus' heads are called Beta and Gamma. They're the heads Zagreus doesn't pet. Presumably, the affectionate central head is called Alpha.
- When he lived with Hades, Skelly avoided Cerberus because he's made of bones, which Cerberus presumably likes to chew on (being a dog).
- According to Skelly, Cerberus doesn't like baths.

Patroclus: Patroclus was a warrior in the Achaean army during the Trojan War and was Achilles' life-long companion and romantic partner. He currently resides in Elysium and is one of the few shades there who does not attack Zagreus, instead offering an assortment of items, much like Sisyphus and Eurydice.

Patroclus: It is possible to interact with Patroclus many times without properly learning his name, even if he comes up in conversations with Achilles. Until his name is revealed, either by reading his Codex entry or via other means (such as speaking to him with Achilles' Myrmidon Bracer equipped) he will be unable to receive gifts and will generally respond to Zagreus coldly or bitterly.

Patroclus - Datos generales: Title: Fallen Warrior
Type: Shade
Keepsake: Broken Spearpoint
Family: Menoetius (Father) Estenele (Mother)
Relations: Achilles (Lover) † Chiron (Former Mentor)
Voice: Ben Prendergast

Patroclus - Characteristics and Personality: Patroclus, the forgotten one, is a former elite warrior who fought in the Trojan War and achieved eternal paradise in Elysium. When Zagreus encounters him, he can be found meditating in his monotonously infernal paradise.
Unlike many of the other shades residing in Elysium, who are utterly obsessed with endlessly fighting amongst themselves in the hopes of gaining eternal glory, Patroclus shows little to no interest in engaging in battle.

Patroclus - Characteristics and Personality: Instead, he views the acts of extreme brutality and savagery of his fellow shades as nothing more than an embarrassment and the work of a bunch of deluded fools desperately trying to cling to the past back when they were still important, rather than that of any truly noble warriors.
He bitterly concludes that Elysium was never meant for any genuinely good people.
Patroclus even goes so far as to say that he would have preferred ending up in the (comparatively) more peaceful Asphodel than Elysium after death, perhaps believing that to be the true paradise.

Patroclus - Characteristics and Personality: Similar to his lover Achilles, it is implied that Patroclus suffers from guilt and self-loathing for the many atrocities he witnessed and committed while alive, and when questioned about his past, he refuses to provide details about the battles he and Achilles fought in. Patroclus is indifferent, stoic, and dislikes small talk. He refers to Zagreus as a "Stranger" and is reluctant to engage with him, initially out of apathy. Achilles explains that this is just how Patroclus is and that he has much less flattering names for people he dislikes, so Zagreus should consider it a compliment.

Patroclus - Characteristics and Personality: Despite being given Achilles' place in Elysium, Patroclus emotionally rejects it and almost shuts himself off, finding his time in Elysium dull without Achilles. Patroclus sits at the edge of the Lethe River, which can erase memories, and contemplates drinking more of it to forget his troubles. He has already taken a few sips, which makes him appear disoriented. He does not reveal his name to Zagreus, possibly as a personal form of escapism. However, he eventually finds the courage to leap into the abyss to retrieve his memories and confront them.

Patroclus - Physical description: Patroclus is an adult male with dark brown skin, with dark hair and a beard, and he often wears a pensive expression.
His hair is adorned with a headband and turquoise leaves, possibly a wreath of glory made of laurel, and he is dressed in battle armor.
His cloak (chlamys) is greenish blue, which matches with the one worn by Achilles, save for the motif on his cloak pin.
His armor is separated by a belt with a Greek meander ornament, and ends in pelvic protecting elongations featuring a wave-like design.
Underneath his armor he wears a white tunic (chiton) covered by a greenish blue wrap (himation) around his waist.

Patroclus - Physical description: His upper right arm features a bandage and the lower one a bracelet, same as his upper left arm.
He is also wearing a single bracer on his left forearm.
His thighs, especially the left one, is wrapped in a strip of bandage as well.
He is barefooted.

Patroclus - Background: Patroclus served valiantly by the side of his beloved companion, Achilles, their bond forged in the midst of the Trojan War. Together, they faced the perils of battle, their hearts entwined in an unbreakable unity. Sadly, tragedy struck, and Patroclus, a courageous warrior, fell on the battlefield.
However, even in death, their souls could not be together. Achilles, driven by a noble impulse, without seeking the counsel of Patroclus, selflessly relinquished his cherished place in the sacred realms of Elysium, bestowing it upon Patroclus, thus separating them.

Patroclus - Hades: Zagreus can come across Patroclus's glade while going through Elysium. At first, he just finds a brooding Patroclus that doesn't even offer his name, claiming names are there to be forgotten. He can learn his name by checking the codex or interacting while having Achilles's Myrmidon Bracer equipped.
From there, Patroclus will confess to feeling abandoned by Achilles and his distaste for Elysium. Zagreus, believing there's something behind the predicament between the two, works to find out and bring the two lovers together again, eventually succeeding.
Patroclus - Hades: With Achilles's contract rewritten, he is now able to visit Patroclus from time to time. Patroclus himself looks in better spirits, as he now has something to look forward to.
Patroclus - Affinity: Patroclus' affinity gauge is maxed out at 8 hearts. The 6th affinity gauge is locked until Zagreus reunites him with Achilles.

Patroclus - Trivia: - His armor differs from the one worn by Achilles, hinting that it's either the one worn by the Myrmidons, who he was part of, or, seeing as his waist armor seems to be richer adorned than the one worn by Achilles, it could be Achilles' old armor which he wore in his stead on the battlefield before he was killed by Hector. [see The Iliad, Bk XVI:1-100 and Bk XVI:101-154]
- The bandages in his design could be a reference to a cup depicting Achilles bandaging Patroclus' arm, by the Sosias Painter (see above-mentioned Wikipedia article).

Patroclus - Trivia: - Being barefooted could underline Patroclus not being at war or "indoors" at the moment.
- Alongside Chaos, Eurydice, Hades and Hermes, Patroclus is one of the few characters to ever comment on someone else's keepsake, namely Achilles'. That is also one of the ways to learn his name.
- Strangely, Patroclus' arm bracer in his standing portrait is mirrored from its position on both his seated portrait and character model.
- In his standing portrait, Patroclus holds his spear in his right hand. While fighting, he uses his left hand.
- Patroclus mentions killing a demigod during a war, a reference to Sarpedon, a son of Zeus.

Patroclus - Trivia: - His and Achilles' Arcana cards, Excellence and The Swift Runner respectively, are designed to be opposites of each other.
Patroclus' shows him in standby, turned to the left, the wheats at the bottom going to the right, the white horse behind the black horse at the top, and it uses cold colors like blues and greens primarily.
The horses seen on the cards could represent both of them; white for Achilles, black for Patroclus.
However, the horses could also be an allusion to Xanthus and Balius, the immortal horses of Achilles, which Patroclus led in his function as Achilles' charioteer.

Patroclus - Trivia: The armor Patrcolus is wearing is in the typical green colors of Achilles and looks very magnificent.
It could be Achilles' armor, as Patroclus' most famous battle was the one he fought in Achilles' stead and in his armor.
Patroclus - Additional notes: For additional information on Patroclus that does not pertain to Hades, see Wikipedia's article: Patroclus

Infernal Trove: Treasure chests worth more the faster you slay the foes guarding them.
Infernal Troves are chests that may occasionally be found in the underworld. They may contain,,, or.
Upon trying to open an Infernal Trove, enemies begin to spawn in. These enemies must be killed quickly, as the reward from the Trove decays slowly the longer the challenge continues. Upon all enemies being killed, the timer freezes, and Zagreus may collect his reward from the Trove.

Infernal Trove - Spawning: Infernal Troves cannot spawn in the first chamber of a biome, in a boss room, or in the chamber immediately following a boss. They will also not spawn in consecutive chambers. They do not spawn naturally in the chambers in Temple of Styx. A Trove Tracker can override these conditions and cause a Trove to spawn regardless, where possible.
Infernal Trove - Extra Drop: In addition to its intended reward, an Infernal Trove can drop a Nectar at a rate of 5% when all the spawned enemies are killed.

Megaera: Megaera is one of the three sisters Furies. She is the older sister of Tisiphone and Alecto, being responsible for punishing adulterers, oathbreakers, and thieves. She is sent by Hades to stop Zagreus from escaping the Underworld. Zagreus must defeat her before progressing to Asphodel during any given escape attempt.

Megaera: After her first defeat, Megaera will join the House of Hades as a character that can be interacted with, though she will still attempt to stop Zagreus from entering Asphodel. She will be found drinking in the House's lounge, but only after a run in which she was defeated; if the lounge has yet to be re-opened, she will instead hang around in the hallway, on the opposite side of Zagreus's door from where Nyx usually stands.

Megaera: Apparently, she has been tasked with handling matters in Tartarus apart from her sisters; this includes dealing with Zagreus. According to Megaera, a war amongst the mortals has made the Underworld particularly busy, and her sisters are handling matters elsewhere.

Megaera - Characteristics and Personality: Megaera is confident, obstinate, and conducts her work with perfection. She has a special hatred for oath-breakers and takes joy in torturing them for eternity. Despite her composure, her pleasure in punishing them is evident.

Megaera - Characteristics and Personality: Megaera disapproves of all the chaos that Zagreus is causing in the Underworld and dislikes his challenging nature. She doesn't want to stop him, but his continued rebellion forces her into a position she hates. Hades trusts her, and her dutiful, law-abiding nature won't stop her from challenging orders if she has a good reason to do so. Zagreus refers to her as his "ex," and both admit that he was responsible. Although Meg does not hold any resentment about it, she will unload her frustration on Zagreus.

Megaera - Characteristics and Personality: When she's off duty, she tends to relax inside the Lounge and interact with other underlings of Hades, notably Dusa, whom she considers her 'best friend'. Among her sisters, she's the most balanced, sane, and calm, and often gets irritated with their mischiefs. Megaera has a cold gaze, but also has a sweet side towards her friends and towards Zagreus. Outside of the battle against her, she is friendly with him and asserts that she is just doing her job, not for personal reasons.

Megaera - Characteristics and Personality: Megaera has a competitive side, taking note of her wins or losses against Zagreus. She doesn't take losing to him well, but her battles against him fuel a friendly rivalry between the two, not a vendetta. Even if Megaera pleads, whether she wants it or not, if she can't handle the task, her younger sisters will be contacted by Hades in her place, which she considers as extreme measures. Despite appearing relentless, even she can have a fragile side. After a stressful day, in the arms of Nyx, she'll express her work-related frustrations.

Megaera - Physical description: Megaera exudes a stern but alluring presence with her yellow eyes, pale blue skin, and slightly darker blue hair pulled back into a long ponytail.
A large, bat-like wing protrudes from the right side of her back, with the inside being black and blue and the outside pink and red.
She has bright pink lips, fingernails, and toenails.
Her attire consists of dark gray and deep blue robes adorned with gold plates on her calves, shoulders, and right wrist.
Additionally, she wears gold earrings, a headpiece, and piercings in her left nostril and eyebrow.
She wears coordinate clothing like her sisters, primarily in shades of blue with gold accents.
Megaera - Physical description: Megaera carries a bright pink leather whip as her weapon of choice.

Megaera - Hades: Megaera, born from the blood of a Titan, was the first of the Furies to emerge from Tartarus. She was created with the purpose of punishing transgressors, thieves, and especially those who committed adultery during their mortal lives.
When Megaera grew up, Nyx, whom she sees as a maternal figure, hired her alongside her sisters, Tisiphone and Alecto, to work in the House of Hades. She has been a longtime friend of Thanatos. At some point, it seems that she had a relationship with Zagreus, which apparently ended. However, Megaera holds no grudges regarding the matter, and she and Zagreus have moved on, leading their respective lives.

Megaera - Hades: Megaera is the only Fury around at first, and Hades orders her to stop Zagreus's escape attempts. After she fails a few times, Hades will turn to her sisters, which greatly displeases her.
With time, Zagreus tries to rebuild a friendship with her, and eventually is successful. This leaves her at a tight spot, since she has to stop Zagreus at Hades's order, but doesn't really hate him and doesn't want him to think so.

Megaera - Hades: A situation may come up where Dusa is fired by Nyx. Since both are close, this greatly angers Megaera, and she reachs out to Zagreus to solve the situation, as he was partly the reason she was fired. Eventually, Dusa is re-hired, and both thank the prince for it.
With the family problems solved, and Zagreus's escape attempts becoming official securities checks, Megaera will continue to appear at the end of Tartarus to try to stop him, but now their fights are more like friendly banter.

Megaera - Affinity: Megaera's affinity gauge is maxed out at 10 hearts. The 6th affinity gauge is locked until Zagreus completes her favor. In order to trigger the first encounter with Megaera in Zagreus' room (to collect her belongings), she must have been gifted at least 4 Nectar.
After a random number of encounters with the Furies, Megaera will approach Zagreus in his room, and tell him that she's only stopping him from escaping because she has to. After this interaction, Megaera can receive Ambrosia the next time she is met in the House of Hades.
It is NOT necessary to enable the "Extreme Measures" condition of the Pact of Punishment.

Megaera - Romance: Reaching maximum affinity with Megaera will allow Zagreus to either begin a romantic relationship with her or continue as friends. Thanatos, Dusa and Megaera can all be romanced at the same time with no negative repercussions.
If Zagreus is able to fully romance both Megaera and Thanatos, another scene will be unlocked in Zagreus’s Room, in which he, Megaera and Thanatos meet up and can begin a polyamorous relationship.

Megaera - Trivia: - Megaera is the only one of the Fury Sisters allowed in the House of Hades.
- When Megaera is off duty, she enjoys spending her time with Zagreus and the other employees in the lounge, especially Dusa, who always keeps her informed about the gossip around the House. Her friendship with Dusa is possibly a reference to how it was said the Furies had snakes for hair.
- Megaera shows affection for bats in general (in a conversation, she mentions that she raises bat pups). The Chthonic Companion she can give to Zagreus is a bat named Battie.

Megaera - Trivia: - The relationship between Megaera and Zagreus is somewhat confusing, as at one point Megaera claims that she and Thanatos have known each other for a long time, even before Zagreus was born.
Some confusion may arise from an item called Portrait, Cerberus, which can be obtained from the Contractor and depicts Megaera, Thanatos, and Zagreus as babies.
However, this item does not depict canonical events as it includes Skelly in the image.
Therefore, the true nature of their relationship remains somewhat unclear.

Megaera - Trivia: Some in-game artwork adds to the confusion by depicting Megaera, Tisiphone, and Alecto as already adult beings emerging from Tartarus, although this may be more consistent within the game.
- If Zagreus fights her with Exagryph, she is shocked that he has the device and says she's always wanted to see it in action.
- When fulfilling the prerequisites to form a bond between Zagreus and Megaera, she becomes an optional auxiliary character he can rely on in combat. However, she cannot be called upon during his clashes with the Furies in the Underworld, as her main goal is to impede Zagreus' escape in the realm.

Megaera - Trivia: - Megaera mentioned that she was born from the blood of a certain Titan, and given the related mythology, she may have been referring to Ouranos. However, it's worth noting that this information is not yet canonical within the game. This would implicitly imply that she and Aphrodite are blood sisters, although it has not been officially confirmed.
- Her relationship with Nyx being that akin to a mother and daughter might come from how in Greek Mythology Nyx was considered the mother of the Erinyes according to some sources.

Megaera - Trivia: - It's implied that Meg channels her frustration from her defeats at Zagreus's hands towards Sisyphus, even though there are numerous reasons why he received his sentence in the Underworld.
Megaera - Additional notes: For additional information on Megaera that does not pertain to Hades, see Wikipedia's article: Megaera

Orpheus: Orpheus is a legendary musician. During his life, he lost his wife and muse Eurydice and ventured to the Underworld to plea for her return. Although he was ultimately unable to bring her back to life, he charmed Hades with his music such that after his death, Hades employed Orpheus as his court musician. However, because he has lost his muse, he is unable to bring himself to sing, though he may be persuaded otherwise.

Orpheus - Datos generales: Title: Court Musician
Type: Shade
Affiliation: House of Hades
Keepsake: Distant Memory
Family: Eurydice (Wife) †
Relations: Apollo (Former Mentor) Hades (Boss)
Voice: Michael Ailshie
Singing Voice: Darren Korb

Orpheus - Characteristics and Personality: A legendary musician, unfortunately, the loss of his wife and musical partner Eurydice deprived Orpheus of any desire to sing, he charms and brings to tears those who listen to him. No one sings a sweeter and sadder song than him.
Despite his reputation for singing sad songs, Orpheus is kind, empathetic, and very friendly, being a good listener to Zagreus. Incredibly, the melancholic Orpheus wasn't always like this; he was full of life and passion for music. However, after his dramatic loss, he became completely devastated and unmotivated to sing, adopting a more bitter and dark personality.

Orpheus - Characteristics and Personality: Poor Orpheus is usually sad and depressed, having completely abandoned his craft after the loss of his muse. Despite still playing and singing, his music sounds more like a personal lament. However, after hearing the epic narrative told by Zagreus, he becomes super inspired and creative, quickly composing a song about it, even though it was just a prank by Dionysus.

Orpheus - Characteristics and Personality: When Zagreus brings news of Eurydice for the first time, and that they can still be reunited, Orpheus doesn't seem to care and prefers to relive his tragic memories, perhaps out of masochism or because it fuels his creativity. Zagreus is quite perplexed by this, but Orpheus actually feels this way because he believes he failed her completely and thinks she's better off without him. In the end, despite both being stubborn about your feelings, Zagreus helps him reunite with her and his mood starts to improve.

Orpheus - Physical description: Orpheus' appearance as a Shade is characterized by pale, sunken skin and extremely unruly dark-green hair. He always has a downcast expression, emphasizing his somber presence. According to Eurydice, this is a relatively younger look for him, as she remembers him having curly hair and a nice tan when they were together, much to Zagreus' surprise.

Orpheus - Physical description: He wears a light purple vest with blue buttons. He wears a brown shawl with golden lining above it, coming from his left shoulder and circulating around his legs. He has some crossed green bracelets on his left wrist, a golden headband and his golden belt is decorated with blue and golden accessories. His nails are purple and he has dark strikes coming down from his green eyes; he also appears to have eyebags. In his right hand, he carries a golden lyre with blue details and three faces engraved in it; it also has some nature motifs in it, such as leaves and tiny flowers.

Orpheus - Hades: Orpheus is a legendary musician who once ventured into the underworld to try to retrieve his wife Eurydice after her untimely death. Although he failed, he was hired by Hades to be the court musician.
By the time of the start of the story, Orpheus has been sent to Tartarus for refusing to sing given his grief, thus not doing his job as court musician. Zagreus is very upset over this, believing it to be an unfair punishment. Hades eventually brings him back to House, and if Zagreus offers him some Nectar, Orpheus will slowly start to sing again.

Orpheus - Hades: During his escape attempts, Dionysus will ask Zagreus to play a little prank on Orpheus to lift his spirits. In doing so, Orpheus will compose the "Hymn to Zagreus", which is filled with the lies and nonsenses the prince fed him. Zagreus tries to explains it is all untrue, but Orpheus feigns ignorance, believing the prince is simply being benevolent and thanks him for the inspiration.

Orpheus - Hades: Zagreus comes into contact with Eurydice, transmitting that information to the musician. Glad to know his wife is doing well, Orpheus is nonetheless hurt to know he is a touchy subject to her, but understands. Upon learning she has created a new song, he requests the prince to retrieve a sheet with it, so he can sing it too. Zagreus is able to obtain the music sheet and hand it to Orpheus, who adds it to his reportory, but sings it slightly differently from Eurydice.
After much back and forth, Zagreus is able to rewrite Orpheus's contract, allowing the musician to visit his wife in Asphodel from time to time.
Orpheus - Hades: Orpheus can be seen either in the House or be found in Asphodel with Eurydice, singing together.

Orpheus - Appearance: Prior to the events of Hades, Orpheus was locked into solitary confinement by Lord Hades due to his refusal to sing. His sentence can be revoked by purchasing the Court Musician's Sentence (which costs 1 Diamond) from the House Contractor. Once revoked, Orpheus will immediately appear in the House of Hades.

Orpheus - Affinity: Orpheus' affinity gauge is maxed out at 8 hearts. After giving him at least 1, Orpheus will begin to sing again, citing Zagreus' determination as inspiration despite the loss of his muse. Thereafter, Orpheus may occasionally be heard singing when Zagreus returns to the House.
As you deepen your relationship with both Orpheus and Eurydice, Zagreus will ask Eurydice for a copy of her song, Good Riddance, which he will share with Orpheus. After receiving the song, Orpheus will begin singing it in the House. After several more conversations with both, Eurydice will begin a meeting with:

Orpheus - Affinity: What happens now, hon...? What I mean is... now you got me thinking about Orpheus again, so... what am I supposed to do with that?
To progress further you will need to have:
- Both Orpheus and Eurydice at a minimum of 5 hearts.
- Access to the Administrative Chamber (purchased through the House Contractor).
- A conversation with Nyx (who must be at 5 hearts) about the Admin Chamber (which can also be triggered by starting Sisyphus's liberation quest).
- A conversation with Hades about Orpheus' contract (which requires Orpheus to have started singing again).

Orpheus - Affinity: - A follow-up conversation with Nyx about Orpheus's sentence, in which she tells you the location of his file in the Admin Chamber.
After finding the document in the Admin Chamber, speak to the House Contractor to purchase the Singer's Gamble for 3 Diamonds.
The next conversation you have with Orpheus will earn his favor and complete the Musician and Muse prophecy in the Fated List of Minor Prophecies.

Orpheus - Trivia: - Orpheus' design appears to be inspired by the character Morpheus from The Sandman comics by Neil Gaiman.
- His "Hymn to Zagreus" song is a direct reference to the Orphic version of Zagreus's myth.
- His "Lament of Orpheus" song is a reference to the song that is said he started singing after failing to rescue Eurydice. This song was said to be so depressing that crops wouldn't grow, pregnant women would have miscarriages, and other misfortunes would happen around him as he sang it.

Orpheus - Trivia: - There are many different versions of the myth, but tradition has it that it was Dionysus that ordered his Maenads to kill Orpheus, offended at how his lamenting affected his worship. For this reason, it's ironic how Dionysus is the one that comes up with an idea to cheer him up. This may stem from the guilt of being the cause of his death in the first place.

Dusa: Dusa is a Shade in the form of a floating, disembodied Gorgon's head. She works as a maid in the House of Hades under Nyx, constantly floating around and cleaning, and after a time is promoted to the House's Head Custodian.

Dusa - Datos generales: Title: Duty-Bound Gorgon
Type: Shade
Affiliation: House of Hades
Keepsake: Harpy Feather Duster
Relations: Zagreus (Crush/"Friend for all Eternity") Megaera (Best Friend/Honorary Sister) Athena (Possible Relationship) Nyx (Employer) Thanatos (Colleague) Hypnos (Colleague)
Voice: Courtney Vineys

Dusa - Characteristics and Personality: Dusa is the severed head of a Gorgon who works as a suffering maid for the House of Hades. She appears very optimistic, cheerful, extremely hardworking and is one of the best people Zagreus could ever meet, but always seems doomed to do everything on her own. Dusa is friendly, shy, playful, a great company and likes to share gossip in her free time. She has a painfully obvious crush on Zagreus (you can even hear some sighs), but she is never able to express her feelings due to her strong social anxiety and, more importantly, her never-ending cleaning tasks.

Dusa - Characteristics and Personality: However, Dusa doesn't like pity and sometimes the residents of the House sympathize with her and offer their help, but she shows her fangs and refuses any assistance, insisting on doing everything on her own. She is a victim of her workload, especially under Nyx's supervision, and gets skittish with anyone she wants to avoid. Dusa is not good at hiding things and can speak without filters. In a conversation with Zagreus, she confesses that she has fantasized about Zagreus and Thanatos in her mind when they are alone, which makes her run away in embarrassment.

Dusa - Characteristics and Personality: At the end of her romance arc, she rejects Zagreus, when he invites her to go out, she realizes that she loves him and admits that he is one of the coolest people in the House of Hades, but she simply doesn't feel attracted him in a romantic way. She asks to remain friends with him for eternity.

Dusa - Physical description: Dusa is a small Gorgon, and her body remains unknown. She has light green skin with freckles and large yellow eyes, giving her a positive expression. One of her serpentine locks always holds a duster, and she ties the emblem of the House of Hades around her forehead.

Dusa - Background: Little is known about Dusa's past, as she doesn't talk much about it.
However, the codex entry on gorgons says that when Medusa was killed, her blood soaked into the underworld and spawned a brood of vengeful offspring.
In a conversation between Zagreus and Dusa where Zagreus asks about Asphodels' gorgons, Dusa says to imagine having mindless siblings made from your own blood.
It can then be assumed that when the hero Perseus decapitated Medusa, her blood soaked into Asphodel and created the gorgons, the Megagorgon, and Dusa.

Dusa - Background: Dusa does specifically say your blood when talking about the gorgons which might mean that Dusa is the soul of Medusa, or perhaps some of Medusa's memory given physical from.
This variation is supported by her reaction to Zagreus asking if she ever had a body, and her statement that the past version of her feels like a different person.
She does mention that she thought anyone could turn others into stone by just looking, like she did.
Her cause of death was decapitation, the preferable method to kill gorgons.

Dusa - Hades: Dusa is a maid in the House of Hades. She's tasked with feeding Cerberus and cleaning the House, occasionally checking on other workers as well. She constantly overworks herself, which often worry those around her. Even if they try to help, she'll just hiss at them and deny their offer.

Dusa - Hades: As Zagreus starts to talk more frequently to her and building a friendship, Nyx grows weary of this, and in what she sees as an act of compassion for the gorgon, fires her. Zagreus doesn't take the news well, and neither does Megaera, so after a little convincing from him, Nyx re-hires Dusa, warning her to not overwork herself so much, and promotes her to Head Custodian.
After the epilogue, she keeps on working for House, now taking better care of herself.

Dusa - Affinity: Dusa's affinity gauge is maxed out at 10 hearts. The 6th affinity gauge will be locked until Zagreus completes Dusa's favor, which involves the lounge renovations, which she has fallen behind on doing. Zagreus must help her bring the lounge up to Nyx's standards by using the House Contractor to complete a minimum of 12 Lounge-focused renovations, which must include at least one rug for the area as well as cleaning up Cerberus's fur and the scratches he left in the floor. After doing this, talking to Dusa will complete the A Place of Revelry prophecy and unlock the ability to give Ambrosia to her.

Dusa - Romance?: Dusa's romance differs from the other options in that each successive gift of Ambrosia requires an increased number of bottles; while her first only requires 1, subsequent gifts require 2, then 3, until her final gift is given as 4 bottles.
After giving Dusa the tenth gift, she and Zagreus will have a conversation where Dusa explains that she has come to realise she isn't looking for an intimate relationship, and isn't attracted to him in that way. They agree to remain "friends for all eternity" instead, though as Zagreus points out, that in itself can be its own form of love.

Dusa - Romance?: Some time after the final romance conversation, Dusa will offer to return all the Ambrosia she has been given; Zagreus may take them back or persuade her to keep them as the gift they were intended as, with no negative repercussions for either choice.
Dusa can be romanced at the same time as Megaera and/or Thanatos with no drawbacks.

Dusa - Trivia: - Dusa's position as a maid in the House of Hades is a play on the name Medusa - she is Maid Dusa.
- The secrecy around Dusa's former life and her claims that she was a very different person when she had a body imply that she might very well be the head of the infamous Medusa. Another hint is that if summoned via her Companion, Dusa gets very nervous seeing Athena when her Greater Call is invoked, as Athena is the one who punished Medusa in many versions of the myth.

Dusa - Trivia: - She seems to have a crush on Zagreus, emitting a gasp and several hearts whenever he gets close. Her conversations are short and flustered, and she often flees into the rafters afterwards. As of the Long Winter update, this relationship can be explored in further detail. Since she rejects Zagreus, realizing she only sees him as a very good friend, the fandom often considers Dusa to be an asexual and/or aromantic character. This hasn't been officially confirmed, however.

Dusa - Trivia: - Nyx disapproves of Dusa for her tendency to overwork herself and associating with Zagreus. She eventually removes Dusa from her job without warning. It is when Zagreus intervenes that Nyx is persuaded to allow Dusa to work in the House again, although not without "certain stipulations".
Dusa - Additional notes: For additional information on Medusa that does not pertain to Hades, see Wikipedia's article: Medusa

Skelly: Skelly is a Bloodless "employed" by the House of Hades as a training dummy. While Skelly claims to be on the House's payroll, he refuses to reveal who hired him and is similarly unwilling to discuss his past, instead preferring to play various pranks on Zagreus. Oddly, no one in the House seems to be aware of his existence besides Zagreus and Achilles, unless the former asks them about him.
Skelly has 900 HP. As he's already dead, he will simply reform after being "killed" in training. He seems suspiciously enthusiastic about getting beaten up.
Skelly: His role is similar to the first game, where he can be used as a training dummy and offer advice on the various game mechanics.

Skelly - Characteristics and Personality: Skelly, the excessively animated skeleton, remains a mysterious figure. Despite lacking flesh and blood, he eagerly assists Zagreus in mastering the use of weapons, serving as a willing punching bag for the prince's practice sessions. Surprisingly, Skelly finds joy in this role, deriving satisfaction from the experience.

Skelly - Characteristics and Personality: Although he is a skeleton, Skelly possesses a vibrant spirit. He is fiercely loyal and courageous, aiding Zagreus in his escapades behind Hades' back. Skelly tends to exhibit extreme behavior, being highly enthusiastic, talkative, and condescending towards those within earshot. He often engages in playful banter, even going as far as pretending to be capable of experiencing death to play pranks on Zagreus, much to the prince's amusement.

Skelly - Characteristics and Personality: Skelly is friendly and helpful by nature, but he has a tendency to quickly develop a sense of familiarity with others, as if he were an expert in the ways of war. Achilles disapproves of Skelly's imprudent advice and questions who Skelly might have been in life to possess such unwavering confidence in death. Additionally, Skelly exhibits a peculiar masochistic inclination, deriving pleasure from enduring blows.

Skelly - Characteristics and Personality: As "Schelemeus", Skelly takes on an almost over-the-top parody of a Drill Instructor training Melinoë and various other Shades on how to defend themselves against Chronos' forces. Though he acts more serious than in Hades, he nonetheless retains his old joking manner and will occasionally lose his stiff demeanor and respond to Melinoë casually.

Skelly - Characteristics and Personality: Skelly’s enigmatic persona is steeped in theatrical charm and deliberate obfuscation. Though he serves as a comic foil and training dummy, his true nature is anything but simple. He delights in spinning contradictory tales about his past, each more absurd than the last, and even the gods—Hermes included—refer to him as a “con artist,” hinting at a possibly criminal life before death. Despite his affable demeanor, Skelly keeps his true origins tightly guarded, even from close allies like Zagreus and Melinoe, suggesting a complex backstory laced with deception, survival, and perhaps redemption.

Skelly - Physical description: Skelly is depicted as a blue-white skeleton with vibrant red eyes, an anatomically upside down nose in the shape of a heart and an expression of excitement. In an interesting departure from typical skeletal appearances, he possesses a few strands of black hair on the top of his head, accompanied by shaggy sideburns and an irregular ridge along his back. Notably, Skelly places a coin with the symbol of the House of Hades in his mouth. This unique combination of features further enhances Skelly's distinct appearance in the game.

Skelly - Physical description: As Schelemeus he looks vastly different from his previous appearance. He now sports a white beard, a headband and his chest is adorned with three medals (gold, silver and bronze). Also, he now wears a long red cape that covers a small part of his right arm, a brown skirt held in place by a silver belt with a crescent moon on it and uses a walking stick. He's no longer hunched back, either, instead standing perfectly straight.

Skelly - Background: Skelly's past is shrouded in mystery. It's implied that he was once a formidable warrior who finally died after surviving numerous legendary battles though none of it has been confirmed.

Skelly - Hades: Skelly first appears right after you purchase your first weapon.
Skelly is shrouded in secrecy, claiming to have been hired by someone who seeks to aid the prince's escape, yet he refuses to disclose the identity of his employer. His actions are driven by a greater purpose, as he plays a part in helping Zagreus reunite with his mother.

Skelly - Hades: When he discovers Zagreus has finally reunited and brought back his mother, Skelly first assumes his job is done and he must find something else to do. However, after Zagreus explains his escape attempts are now official security checks and he could use some help, Skelly stays to help the Prince get even better at fighting.

Skelly - Hades: Zagreus will repeatedly try to convince Skelly to spill out who he is working for, having discovered it's not anyone from the House, but Skelly will always evade the question, even playing a little prank on the prince by providing a fake backstory. Only when Zagreus threatens to stop beating him does Skelly reveals he is working for Charon. Although shocked by the revelation, Zagreus figures the boatman has his own motives, and Skelly agrees.

Skelly - Challenge Statues (Hades): Skelly will add 3 covered statues to the southwest of the courtyard which require you to complete runs at certain heat levels: 8, 16, and 32.

Skelly - Trivia: - Skelly having an obol in his mouth is a reference to how people in Ancient Greece were buried: with an obol in their mouth so they can pay Charon their passage.
- A recurring theory is that Skelly's true identity is that of Greek hero Odysseus.
Famous for having presented himself as Nobody to the Cyclops Polyphemus, Skelly pulls a similar prank when he refers to himself as Schelemeus.

Skelly - Trivia: Furthermore, Achilles is the only one besides Zagreus to be 100% aware of his existence, and even states he seems to be an expert in the ways of war, while Odysseus has fought in many wars, especially the Trojan War, and was a fellow companion of Achilles.
During his lie about his past, Skelly says he was the "Captain of the Cretan second fleet, sailing to Athens under King Minos"; while this isn't true, Odysseus is very famous for his long trip back home to Ithaca.
Nonetheless, it is referenced in a dialogue with Odysseus, when he says Schelemeus feats rival his own.

Skelly - Trivia: Were this theory to be true, that would mean Skelly is none other than Hermes' great-grandson in Greek Mythology, which could further explain his prankster personality, since Hermes is the God of Trickery.
This could also further explain how they know each other, given their kinship and the times Hermes helped Odysseus, and it might have even been through Hermes that Skelly got hired by Charon.
Additionally, Odysseus infiltrated the Underworld, so Charon would already be slightly aware of the type of person he is.

Skelly - Trivia: - When speaking with Hades as a prisoner and he laments the capture of Nyx, Melinoë will mention Hypnos survived, as well as Schelemeus from his court. Hades will say he has no recollection of such a person, whether it's because of the new name or the fact only the siblings are able to interact with him isn't clear.

Persephone: Persephone is the Goddess of Verdure, the biological mother of Zagreus and Melinoë, and the daughter of Demeter and a Mortal Farmboy.
Originally from Olympus, she eventually married Hades and ruled alongside him as Queen of the Underworld, before mysteriously leaving one day after Zagreus was born. Following her departure, Hades forbade all mentions of her in the House, causing her eldest child to grow up unaware of his mother’s identity.

Persephone: After returning to the Underworld, Persephone and Hades decided to have another child, Melinoë. Unfortunately Persephone did not get the opportunity to raise her either, as the Queen was soon captured by Chronos, along with Zagreus and several of the House of Hades’ staff members. Frozen in time, Persephone would soon be released by an older Melinoë, and return to her rightful place as queen.

Persephone - Characteristics and Personality: Persephone, in contrast to her husband, is openly loving, resilient, fair, sociable, and courageous. When she resided on Olympus, she could not stand the blustering and posturing, nor her mother’s overbearing nature. Persephone values sincerity, and thus could not bear the constant fights, lies, and betrayals of the Olympians. Because of this, when she was taken to the Underworld, she was content to make a life in her new surroundings.

Persephone - Characteristics and Personality: Since become queen, she proved to be a great powerful leader, making the dark Underworld a more productive and inviting place. She treats others as equals, praise their good work, and overall brings out the best in them. Because of her affable, reliable and respectable nature, she is loved by almost everyone in the Underworld, who were saddened by her sudden departure. Persephone is also resourceful, and adept at adapting to new situations, whether it was becoming queen of the Underworld or making a new home for herself on the surface.

Persephone - Characteristics and Personality: Persephone is very warm and affectionate towards her children, Zagreus and Melinoë, as well as the family dog, Cerberus. As for her husband, Persephone saw beyond Hades' stern demeanor and saw someone honest and respectful. Despite their different dispositions and interests, the two grew to love the other, got married, had a son, and soon had a daughter (despite initially claiming that one child was plenty).

Persephone - Physical description: Persephone has the appearance of a middle-aged woman. She has fair skin, green eyes, and pale blond hair. Her hair bears similarities to Zagreus' hair, and it is tied together with a green ribbon and two lavender plants are tucked into it. When on the surface, she wears a simple dress that is tied with a green ribbon. A rope is also tied in an X on her chest and on her shoulders. She also wears a green shawl, and simple golden bracelets, along with a silver one. She holds a basket full of vegetables on one arm.

Persephone - Physical description: In the family portrait, she wears a much longer dress with gold accents, a red and black detailed sash around her waist, and a green ribbon is seen. Her hair is untied, and she wears red and gold earrings that look similar to bloodstones. She wears the same fiery laurels Hades and Zagreus wears.

Persephone - Physical description: As Queen of the Underworld, she wears a long black dress with white and gold stripes. Around her waist is a belt with a skull with jewel eyes and mouth, and a red and gold cape-like shawl. Two skulls with golden teeth and eyes adorn her shoulders. She wears more jewelry, including a red bracelet, golden rings, golden bracelets, and a necklace bearing the symbol of Hades. Her hair is tied with the green ribbon from her surface attire, but it is now raised to resemble a cornucopia. Her crown has a skull on top, and she again wears the fiery laurels.

Persephone - Physical description: Additionally, she wears an orange shirt underneath her dress. Her hair is now tied with a ponytail that rests on her right shoulder. She wears less extravagant jewelry compare to her previous Queen outfit, only keeping her fiery laurels, golden gorget and red earrings.

Persephone - Background: Persephone’s birth was the result of a union between the agricultural goddess Demeter and a mortal farmer.
The two loved their daughter very much, Demeter affectionately calling her “ Kore ”, and were very happy until Persephone’s father passed, which saddened Demeter greatly.
Although Persephone inherited her mother’s immortality, Demeter feared her daughter was weak due to her mortal heritage.
So she raised her in a protective way that Persephone came to see as overbearing.
This, as well as the constant arrogance, deceit and cruelty amongst the Olympians, gave Persephone an increasing desire to leave.
Persephone - Background: Zeus, aware of Persephone’s frustration and Hades’ feelings towards her, abducted Persephone and gave her to his brother “as a gift”.

Persephone - Background: Hades was obviously horrified and disgusted by his brother’s actions, and feared the consequences that could come should Demeter and the other Olympians discover the Goddess of Verdure’s whereabouts. However, Persephone did not wish to return to Olympus, so Hades, rather than send her away, gave the goddess the solace to do as she pleased, granting her freedom and autonomy, whilst staying silent on the true nature of her disappearance to avoid conflict with Olympus. Unbeknownst to Persephone, Hades’ fear was well founded, as Demeter, full of grief, anger and desperation to find her daughter, unleashed an "Endless Winter", causing famine and harsh snowy climate amongst mortals.

Persephone - Background: Overtime, a genuine love formed between Persephone and the King of the Underworld.
They soon married, with Persephone becoming an exceptional queen, and the two eventually had a child together.
Unfortunately, the child, Zagreus, died at birth.
Inconsolable, Persephone abdicated her throne as the Queen of the Underworld, and left to live a new life on the surface, hidden from Olympus with the help of her companion, Nyx.

Persephone - Background: Her disappearance left many of the Underworld’s residents distraught, Hades especially, to the point that he forbade any mention of her, causing Zagreus, who was revived thanks to Nyx, to be unaware of his mother’s identity, and receive constant mistreatment from his father, whose despair manifested as anger.

Persephone - Hades: An older Zagreus discovers Persephone’s existence through a letter she left behind (as well as Homer’s narration). When Hades refused to divulge any information about her, this proves to be the final impetus for Zagreus. He becomes determined to escape the Underworld, find his mother and hopefully get some answers.

Persephone - Hades: After successfully escaping, Zagreus meets Persephone at her secret home on the surface: a cottage with a garden by the coast. Persephone does not recognize him, and reacts with disbelief and anger when he claims himself as her son, thinking it must be a cruel trick. Persephone becomes emotional, revealing to Zagreus that he died at birth, his burning feet sputtering out. Now believing his identity, she reacts with joy in seeing her son alive.

Persephone - Hades: The two spend time together, Zagreus telling her about his journey to the surface, and informing her that Cerberus is doing well (as requested by his father when he was defeated). Persephone then asks him what convinced him to find her, only for Zagreus to suddenly begin to weaken. He assumes it is the weather on the surface affecting him, as he is unaccustomed to it, but Persephone explains that, like his father, he is bound to the Underworld, and must return there. Before Zagreus sinks into the River Styx, Persephone asks that he comes back, however long it takes.

Persephone - Hades: In the next meeting, Persephone says that she never felt that she belonged in the Underworld, despite the efforts of those within it to be welcoming. According to the Fates, a child born of surface dwellers could not survive in the Underworld, but Persephone and Hades attempted to have a child anyway. Overcome by grief from Zagreus emerging stillborn, she left the Underworld.

Persephone - Hades: Hades later reveals that the Fates said he would have no heir, and that it was through Nyx's efforts that he survived, likely convincing the Fates to spare him from death. Before he dies, he asks if Persephone would have returned had she known he lived, to which she responds that she would have gone through hell to see him.

Persephone - Hades: Zagreus later suggests that Hades is protecting Persephone since she cannot be seen by the Olympians. She is surprised to know that Zagreus is aware of this, and later they make the conclusion that Hades believes that, by not letting Zagreus see her, she will be safe from the Olympians, still unaware of where she is, preventing a war. As Zagreus begins to weaken, Persephone sounds regretful for her actions.

Persephone - Hades: The next meeting starts with her requesting that Zagreus does not return to her afterwards, both for her safety and his. Zagreus is upset by this and argues with her, but she tells him that Hades must know what he is doing and that both of their safety is at risk whenever he visits. When returning in the next run, Persephone will tell him to leave again, but is stopped by him telling her that Hades still loves her. Before dying, he says that knowing she is safe is not enough and that their family is stuck together and has to work through their problems.

Persephone - Hades: After Zagreus showed his mother proof that Hades still loves her, Persephone remained hesitant to return to the Underworld. However, during Zagreus’ final attempt to reach her, he finds her packing her things, having decided to return after all, with Charon rowing both her and Zagreus back on the River Styx.

Persephone - Hades: Upon their return, Persephone opens the gates to the House of Hades, where, inside, Hades and Cerberus are waiting for them. She happily greets Cerberus and reconnects with Hades, and tells him to apologize to their son. She then tells her family her plan to resolve the conflict with Olympus, but needs both of them to cooperate. To keep appearances up, Zagreus is permitted to continue his attempts to escape the Underworld, now officially acting as a security specialist, while Persephone plans.
After bonding with the Olympians, Persephone will task Zagreus with sending out invitations to each one.

Persephone - Hades: She reveals that her plan is to invite the Olympians to a party, where she will reveal herself to them.
Purposefully not mentioning Zeus’ involvement, Persephone will instead claim that she eloped with Hades to the Underworld, where she had a son that soon sought out his extended family.
She will then state that, after being moved by his numerous attempts to escape, she and Hades decided to finally reach out.

Persephone - Hades: Zagreus expresses concern for Persephone's elaborate lie, but she assures him that their relatives will likely know she will is not being entirely truthful, but they will still be willing to let go of the past, and move on with no hard feelings.

Persephone - Hades: During the party, Persephone and Demeter reunited. Demeter's response was mixed, as she was overjoyed to see her daughter safe and happy, but also wanted Persephone to return to the surface and to her responsibilities. When Zagreus learns of this, he fears that she is leaving permanently, but Persephone assures him that she will return. During some of the runs that follow, Persephone will be absent, having left to visit Olympus, but will return to the house eventually.

Zagreus's Room: The second available chamber in the House of Hades, this cluttered room was the Prince's bedchamber before he began his futile attempts to escape. The room contains an imposing mirror, an empty desk, a large bed, four bookshelves, two chairs, two overstuffed chests, and miscellaneous clutter. Notable among the clutter are three massive skulls, accompanied by a smaller skull and a display board of an additional six smaller skulls. They appear to resemble the skulls of Cyclopes, Gorgons, and some large-mawed beast. The player can choose to add more to this room by purchasing décor from the House Contractor using Gemstones and a Diamond.

Zagreus's Room - The Mirror of Night: Dominating the top-left wall of Zagreus' room is the Mirror of Night, a rectangular slab of mirrored-doom several times Zagreus's height. It has a beautifully gilded frame embedded with gems of crystallized Darkness.

Zagreus's Room - Zagreus' Desk: A finely crafted desk on the left wall of Zagreus's room. It appears with three scrolls of parchment, an ink pot supplied with an over-sized orange feather, and what seem to be several dishes from previous meals. After purchasing the relevant upgrade from the House Contractor for 20, this desk will become adorned with the Fated List of Minor Prophecies.

Zagreus's Room - Zagreus' Bed: This well-made and surprisingly tidy bed dominates the right side of Zagreus's room. Though imaginably quite comfy, Zagreus will typically refuse to sleep, ever-focused on his next escape. It receives the same response that chairs elsewhere in the house are given, humorously implying that Zagreus would rather sit on it rather than lay down. On certain occasions, Zagreus will state that he wishes to lie down. As Zagreus dreams, a flashback sequence will begin.

Zagreus's Room - Chthonic Bedding: This bedding is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 150. After its purchase, it will alter the look of the bed, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus will then remark that he's already bought it so there's no need for the narrator to sell him on it.

Zagreus's Room - Scrying Pool: This mystical water-filled bowl is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 10. It retroactively records the number of escape attempts and foes killed in the current save file and will update after each attempt. After its purchase, it will appear in Zagreus's room next to the exit to the courtyard, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus will then remark that he's wanted one of his own for some time.

Zagreus's Room - Trojan Arms: The assorted weaponry, leftovers from the Trojan War that found their way into the Underworld, is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 200. It decorates the space above Zagreus' bed. Displayed there include a bronze shield emblazoned with the crest of Hades, a bronze dagger with a decorated crossguard, and strangely enough - a pair of nunchucks. Zagreus remarks that the mortals who created these weapons had the right idea, though their products are on the crude side.

Zagreus's Room - Achilles Wall-Scroll: This illustration of the valiant hero Achilles, from his days as commander of the Greek forces during the Trojan War, is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 60. After its purchase, it will appear in Zagreus' room between the mirror and the exit to the courtyard, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus remarks that his mentor must have been incredible back when he was alive.

Zagreus's Room - Aphrodite Wall-Scroll: This full-body illustration of the lovely goddess Aphrodite, in her full splendor upon first arriving at the island of Kythera, is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 120. After its purchase, it will appear in Zagreus' room between the exit to the courtyard and his bed, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus then wonders if he could get it signed.

Zagreus's Room - Dionysus Wall-Scroll: This illustration of Dionysus is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 80. After its purchase, it will appear in Zagreus' room above the Scrying Pool, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus then remarks it's like he and Dionysus share a bond.

Zagreus's Room - Fancy Recliner: This blue and gold recliner is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 50. After its purchase, it will appear in Zagreus' room to left of the exit to the courtyard, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus then remarks he simply prefers to stand.

Zagreus's Room - Massive Weights: These golden weights and dumbbells are items available for purchase from the House Contractor for 430. After their purchase, they will appear in Zagreus' room to the right of the entrance to the chamber, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus then retorts that he gets a lot of exercise.

Zagreus's Room - Splendid Lyre: This golden lyre standing on a stone pedestal is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 1. After its purchase, it will appear in Zagreus' room to the right of the little bookcase at the foot of his bed, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus then remarks it can't be that hard to play.

Zagreus's Room - Entertainment Table: This gilded wooden table topped with a game is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 430. After its purchase, it will appear in Zagreus' room at the foot of his bed. Zagreus then retorts that the narrator should face him himself.

Zagreus's Room - Stately Rug: This black rug woven with golden patterns is an item available for purchase from the House Contractor for 20. After its purchase, it will appear in Zagreus' room in the centre of the chamber, after a brief quip from the narrator. Zagreus then remarks he guesses it is soft.

Pact of Punishment: The Pact of Punishment is a contract provided by Hades for the purpose of making Zagreus' escape attempts even more difficult while earning valuable rewards. In a regular playthrough (save file), the Pact will only appear after the Final Boss is defeated at least once, and Zagreus has claimed victory. When he inevitably returns to the House of Hades, the Pact of Punishment will block the open window in the courtyard, allowing Zagreus to customize aspects of his run before he leaves. In Hell Mode, the Pact is available from the start and in fact cannot be fully disabled.

Pact of Punishment - In-game info: NOTICE: Congratulations!! Your deeds have compelled Lord Hades to serve you a Pact of Punishment. Here is how it works:
- The Pact can make escaping more difficult via various nasty Conditions
- Each Condition you accept adds some Heat to your Heat Gauge
- While your Heat Gauge is full, you can earn valuable Bounties!
You earn one Bounty the first time you vanquish the boss of each Underworld region while your Heat Gauge is full. Once you successfully escape, you can earn more Bounties... if you turn up the Heat
Pact of Punishment - In-game info: Hint: You can earn Bounties for each weapon! How much Heat you need is per-weapon, as well. If things get too hot, try switching weapons.

Pact of Punishment - Conditions: The Pact of Punishment features a total of 15 (16 in Hell Mode) different conditions which can affect an escape attempt. Most of these have differing levels, allowing Zagreus to further increase how effective one condition is.
Each Condition in the Pact of Punishment is worth a certain amount of Heat. The amount of Heat displayed in the gauge on the left of the Pact's UI represents the "total difficulty" of the conditions chosen.

Pact of Punishment - Conditions: Choose your conditions for a run carefully. Many of the conditions can be nearly ineffective against one particular weapon build, but extremely difficult to another, yet can also run into unexpected difficulties (or lack thereof) based upon a run's Boons. The prophecy Harsh Conditions requires you to completely clear a run with each of the conditions in place, but the condition only needs a single rank active in it, and they do not need to be done all on the same weapon or within a single run.

Pact of Punishment - Convenience Fee: Affects all items from Charon's Shops, Wells of Charon, with the exception of the Diamond or Titan Blood offered in the Temple of Styx.

Pact of Punishment - Extreme Measures: Affects one boss for each level. At Level 1, it only affects the Furies. At Level 2, it also affects the Bone Hydra. At Level 3, it also affects Theseus and Asterius, including Asterius's solo appearance as a mini-boss. At Level 4, also affects the Final Boss. See the appropriate pages for details.
If Zagreus has not encountered all three of the Furies, Extreme Measures is hidden and cannot be selected. Extreme Measures Level 4 (Extremer Measures) can only be purchased from the House Contractor after the main game is completed and the Final Boss is fought an additional time.

Pact of Punishment - Benefits Package: Affects armored enemies, granting them one additional perk up to a max of 2 per level. The perks are:
- Shifter (green ghost) - The enemy will teleport randomly.
- Bruiser (helm) - The enemy has greatly increased health and size.
- Slugger (sword) - The enemy deals more damage, like the Hard Labor punishment. (Stacks with other pacts of punishment).
- Puller (purple disk) - The enemy has a small 'gravitational' field around them that can not be escaped by walking. Usually takes several dashes to break free.

Pact of Punishment - Benefits Package: - Savior (blue shield) - The enemy will periodically give other nearby enemies 1 shielded health, up to a max of 5.
- Speeder (boots) - The enemy attacks and moves faster, like the Forced Overtime punishment. (Stacks with other pacts of punishment).
- Linker (pink ray) - A laser is created from the enemy to another nearby enemy. Prioritizes linking with armored foes, but can link to normal enemies.
- Cloner (skulls) - Tartarus only. Fake clones of the enemy will constantly spawn, up to a cap. Each clone has 1 hp (armor and regular each). All clones die when the original dies.

Pact of Punishment - Benefits Package: - Burner (fire) - Asphodel only. The enemy will constantly create fire traps.
- Seeker (green star) - Projectiles fired by this enemy will home in on you.
- Popper (warrior soul) - Exalts in Elysium only. In addition to the real soul, the Exalt will drop several fake souls that explode upon death or after a few seconds.

Pact of Punishment - Middle Management: Adds a unique effect to each and every mini-boss Encounter.
- The Wretched Sneak in Tartarus summons Wringers.
- The Doomstone has a new arena featuring Chimera traps on several islands.
- The mini-boss room in Tartarus has increased numbers (4 enemies instead of 2) and the chosen enemies are a random mix of Slam-Dancers, Inferno-Bombers, Burn-Flingers, and Wave-Makers, instead of 2 of the same enemy.
- The Barge of Death Encounter in Asphodel summons a Dire Voidstone (with increased health) alongside a horde of enemies. There is only one wave of enemies.

Pact of Punishment - Middle Management: - The Witches Circle encounter in Asphodel gives its Dire Spreaders a new attack: firing four shielded orbs in a cross that cannot be destroyed by Zagreus's attacks.
- The Megagorgon and Elite Skull-Crusher Encounter in Asphodel gives both enemies new abilities. The Megagorgon gains the ability to frequently teleport around the room, and the Skull-Crusher's landing creates a shockwave that travels across the entire room, and must be dashed through to avoid.
- The Elite Soul Catcher Encounter in Elysium gains the ability to dash elsewhere in the room at regular intervals.

Pact of Punishment - Middle Management: - The solo Asterius encounter in Elysium is unaffected by Middle Management. Instead, he is affected by Extreme Measures if it is enabled at Level 3.
- The final rooms of Elite wings in the Temple of Styx will have 2 different Dire enemies in the room, instead of 1.
Mini-bosses summoned by the Final Boss during his boss fight also receive the extra abilities mentioned above.

Pact of Punishment - Underworld Customs: Zagreus must use the Pool of Purging provided in the staircase room between region to purge at least one Boon. He still receives the normal amount of Obols in exchange.
If Zagreus does not have any Boons, he can proceed anyway.

Pact of Punishment - Tight Deadline: After the time runs out, Zagreus takes 5 damage every second while the timer is running. That damage cannot be reduced in any way, not even by invulnerability. When Zagreus enters a new biome, Tight Deadline will add the stipulated duration to the timer.
The timer will pause:
- After a region's boss has been defeated, as well as in the transition staircase rooms between biomes.
- In the first empty room of a region (with the exception of the first room in Tartarus).
- During all Thanatos encounters.
- While in a non-combat chamber with Sisyphus, Eurydice, or Patroclus.
- While fishing.
- While choosing a boon or upgrade.

Pact of Punishment - Tight Deadline: - While the codex is open (the timer will not pause until the text has loaded, however).
- During cutscenes.
- While the game is paused.
Chambers where Zagreus must survive for a set duration against continually spawning enemies will not appear while Tight Deadline is active.

Pact of Punishment - Routine Inspection: Zagreus does not start with any uses of Fated Authority or Fated Persuasion, though if he gains dice through Chthonic Keys with the Fated Keys work order, the talent selected by the Mirror still determines which one he can use.
If the Mirror of Night has not been fully unlocked, Routine Inspection is hidden and cannot be selected.

Pact of Punishment - Rewards: Defeating the Final Boss at certain Heat thresholds (8, 16, and 32) unlocks special rewards - though much to the disappointment of Zagreus (and perhaps also the player), these "rewards" are merely cosmetic statues of Skelly to display in the House of Hades courtyard.
In addition, powering the Pact up to 5, 10, and 15 Heat will allow Zagreus to access the Infernal Gates that lead to Erebus in Tartarus, Asphodel, and Elysium, respectively.

Pact of Punishment - Bounties: In addition to the rewards above, completing the game with active Heat will award Zagreus with bounties. Each boss slain at (or above) a Target Heat value will drop a Diamond, an Ambrosia or Titan Blood which Zagreus can spend back in the House of Hades. After defeating the Final Boss and achieving victory at the target Heat value, the target will be raised for future bounties.
Bounties and Target Heat are tracked independently per weapon.

Pact of Punishment - Bounties: The limit for bounties is 20 Heat, with 21 completed runs that need to be completed to collect all bounties. In Hell Mode, bounties start at 5 heat, and the limit is increased to 25 Heat.
Bounties can only be collected once per weapon, per boss, per Heat level. So for example, once a player has defeated the Furies on 3 Heat with the Sword, they will no longer be able to collect a Bounty from defeating them with the Sword until they also defeat the Final Boss. However, the player can still collect a Bounty for defeating the Furies with a different weapon.

Pact of Punishment - Bounties: You can only claim rewards for the lowest Heat you have not yet completed, even if you defeat a boss at a higher heat (e.g If you have not yet beaten the Final Boss on 2 Heat for the Rail, then you go through and defeat them using 5 Heat, you will claim the remaining rewards for 2 Heat, and your Target Heat for the Rail will go up to 3). The Bounties for 0 Heat are tracked separately, and cannot be claimed by clearing on a higher heat.

Hell Mode: Hell Mode is a harder difficulty option that may be selected when creating a new save file. This option cannot be changed later and disables God Mode from use. Selecting Hell Mode has Zagreus start the game with the Pact of Punishment immediately in use. The Pact of Punishment has five mandatory conditions with one Hell Mode exclusive condition, Personal Liability, which removes the impervious shield that Zagreus briefly gains upon taking burst damage.
Hell Mode offers bounties up to 25 heat instead of 20 heat in normal difficulty, due to the mandatory 5 heat from the start.

Hell Mode - Mandatory Conditions: The Pact of Punishment in Hell Mode has one rank in each of five mandatory conditions.
Further ranks of these conditions can be added and removed freely.

Wretched Sneak: It will generally attack in a pattern of a few dart throws, then a melee jab. After this jab, the Sneak dusts off its hands and is quite vulnerable to damage. How many cycles of darts the Sneak throws is random, but it is generally at least two. The Sneak moves through teleporting. These teleports remove any status curses that Zagreus may be able to inflict.
When Middle Management is turned on, it periodically summons Wringer reinforcements from the sides of the chamber, potentially swarming Zagreus if he does not take them down.

Combat Style: Varies

It fires an 8-line radial pattern of beams from itself, beginning with two beams and sequentially firing more, though only 6 can be active at a time.
Each time it takes damage, the Doomstone releases a Fragment that can form barriers of beams when near each other or the main Doomstone, similar to the Linker trait from the Benefits Package Pact condition. The Fragments each have 20 Health and 20 Armor, and their beams deal 1 Damage per tick.

Skull-Crusher - Combat: When a Skull-Crusher spots the player, they will immediately take to the skies and hover above Zagreus. A shadow will appear where they will fall, following the player until they briefly stop moving. If the player stops moving while being tracked by a Skull-Crusher, the Skull-Crusher will slam to their ground after a brief delay. The area of effect is a bit larger than one might expect, so two dashes are recommended to properly evade one.

Skull-Crusher - Combat: Skull-Crushers almost never attack without the player coming to a rest; if you keep moving they can be convinced never to land. This gives time to deal with other onscreen enemies, but can make killing them take longer than expected. Without armor they can be stunned while on the ground like other enemies.
A singular armored Skull-Crusher (previously an endlessly respawning non-armored Skull-Crusher) accompanies the Megagorgon as the Asphodel mini-boss. In that encounter, the Skull-Crusher provides the brunt of the damage while the Megagorgon assists with petrifying missiles.

A Dire Soul Catcher, referred to as the Butterfly Ball by Zagreus, appears only as a miniboss encounter in Elysium and is much larger than normal Soul Catchers. In addition to spawning butterflies, it will constantly spawn Elite Disarmed Souls, up to five, that will seek out the sword, spear, shield, and two bows littered around its arena. Under the Middle Management pact, it will also periodically teleport around the room.

Pool of Purging: The Pool of Purging is an interactable object that can be found in the Underworld. In it, Boons can be washed away and converted into Obols.

Alecto: Alecto is one of the three sisters Furies. She is the younger sister of Megaera and Tisiphone, she does not initially appear in the game, as both she and Tisiphone are busy with matters in the mortal world. Alecto is responsible for punishing those who allow their passions to drive them to terrible acts.
After Megaera has been defeated a certain amount of times, Alecto and Tisiphone will begin appearing, randomly replacing her at the end of Tartarus. Alecto does not appear in the House of Hades after she has been defeated.

Type: Chthonic Goddess
